```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a clearly identified payer, the primary adult-child caregiver. At least four sourced competitors charge them directly at $3.99–$24.99/month (SplitKin, CircleCare, CompassCare, Caring Village), so consumer willingness to pay in this category is shown by live pricing. Idea B's brief states 'No clean single payer found,' and every named competitor is free to the end user.",
    "The 90-day paying-customer goal favors A. A consumer can subscribe on day one with no data-density prerequisite. B needs enough hazard data in at least one city before it is useful, and its proposed payers (municipalities, advocacy nonprofits, grants) imply long institutional sales cycles that the brief does not source or size.",
    "A's demand evidence is closer to end users: Reddit caregivers describe current workarounds such as Google Sheets and group texts. B's demand evidence comes from a single HN seed quote, a nonprofit's marketing copy, and a competitor founder's origin story. None of these shows anyone willing to pay.",
    "B's only consumer-monetized analog, Pointz, needed $520k in outside funding and does not publish its price. That is evidence against a solo operator reaching revenue quickly.",
    "A's risks are real: six or more direct competitors, a user quote saying 'as long as it's free,' short customer lifetime, multi-sibling activation friction, and FTC/WA MHMDA compliance. These risks mostly limit the scale of A. They do not block a first paying customer, whereas B's lack of a payer does."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's claimed 'credible non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants)' in its Case For has no source. The brief cites no municipality or advocacy group paying a third-party vendor for this, and its own Open Questions ask whether cities would pay at all. The only funding evidence is a $930k government grant to a research project, which is not a purchase a solo company could repeat.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderately high confidence that A is the better first bet, mainly because B has no evidenced payer. A's case still has gaps: there is no sourced conversion or CAC data for a new entrant, no defined differentiating wedge against 6+ competitors, and some direct evidence that target users resist paying. A's first paying customer is plausible within 90 days, but sustainable unit economics are unproven."
}
```
